perItemFindings.one_line: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.

verbatim_critique:
[D0.5.G cold referee] delivered tier=subfield below novelty_target=field (floor=field). The delivered theorems establish exact optimization and certificates when the relevant full-graph component has cycle rank zero or one, plus NP-completeness for deterministic binary endogenous chains with shared exogenous roots. The repeated description as a "frontier" is stronger than proved: the hardness construction is not shown to have relevant full-graph cycle rank two, or any fixed rank above one, so the note does not establish a cycle-rank dichotomy or maximal tractability boundary. The positive and negative results are therefore separate tractability and hardness regimes rather than matching sides of the advertised parameterized frontier. The NP-hardness argument also uses the classical bounded-clause SAT lemma without a precise citation, while the claimed backend significance is unsupported by a delivered implementation or reproducible experimental artifact; these omissions constrain the leading-journal score. [D0.5.G projected paper-score gate: paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'. The score assesses the delivered research package without credit for unfinished work.]

HALTED AT TRIAGE: the math panel returned `revise` and its findings were never repaired, so this note is NOT established as mathematically sound — do not bank it as downgraded on this verdict alone. Open findings: negative_counterexample_nondegeneracy@prop:full-endogenous-separation, ballast_duplicate_corollary@prop:endogenous-causal-tree-np-completeness, ballast_immediate_corollary@thm:global-unicycle-polynomial-corollary
